title: United States military announces dismantling of the Gaza aid pier
body:
On 17 July 2024, the United States military announced that the floating pier it had built off the Gaza coast to deliver humanitarian aid would be dismantled. The pier was installed on the Gaza shore on 16 May 2024, and aid trucks first crossed it on 17 May. Nine days after installation, bad weather broke it apart and it was taken to the Israeli port of Ashdod for more than two weeks of repairs.

Aid distribution from the pier was halted on 8 June 2024 after an Israeli military raid that rescued four hostages in Nuseirat, and the pier was detached for the final time on 28 June. It operated for fewer than 25 days, and aid agencies used it for about half of that time. The US military said it delivered close to 20 million pounds, or 9 million kilograms, of supplies. USAID said enough aid came through to feed 450,000 people for a month.

Repeated bad weather and security problems, including Israeli military operations near the pier and attacks on aid convoys, hampered distribution, and some aid piled up onshore because agencies had difficulty moving it. The US military said the mission was complete and shifted its focus to a new route for aid through the Israeli port of Ashdod. Critics called the project a 230 million dollar boondoggle.
